image_description: A close-up, high-resolution portrait of a male Mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The image focuses on the head and upper chest, showcasing the iridescent green head, white neck ring, yellow bill with a black tip, and brown chest plumage. The background is blurred water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat. It exhibits the characteristic yellow coloration with a dark tip, matching the description for a Mallard drake.
The eye is clearly visible and appears dark brown/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows dense, smooth plumage typical of waterproof feathers. The posture suggests buoyancy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic Mallard breeding plumage: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brownish/chestnut chest. This matches the 'Mallard' specific description in the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged or outside the frame of this close-up headshot. They cannot be evaluated.
The wings are largely occluded by the angle and framing. Only the shoulder area is visible, making it impossible to verify the full shape of the wings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame of this close-up shot.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The very tip of the bill has a slight blueish/purple discoloration that is not typical for a Mallard (usually black or dark grey). Additionally, the edge where the bill meets the water shows slight softness/bleeding, though this could be depth-of-field.

The white neck ring fades into the green head and brown chest with slightly unnatural smoothness, lacking the distinct feather boundary texture seen in high-res macro photography, suggesting potential AI smoothing.
